newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Baku rejects Turkmen claims to Caspian reserves.
newsitem.headline: Baku rejects Turkmen claims to Caspian reserves.

text.p: The Foreign Ministry of Azerbaijan on Thursday rejected claims by Turkmenistan to some oil reserves located in the "Azeri sector" of the Caspian Sea.
"Methods of defining the economic border clearly show that the Azeri and Chirag oil structures lie completely within the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea," a ministry statement said.

The Azeri ministry called for talks with Turkmenistan on defining borders and said other potential oilfields -- not including the Azeri and Chirag fields -- between the Azeri and Turkmen sectors could possibly be shared by both sides.
"The Azeri side stresses that in the zone between the Azeri and the Turkmen sectors there are some possible oil structures which could belong to both national sectors," it said.
The Turkmen foreign ministry said earlier on Thursday the Azeri oilfield and part of the Chirag field were located in the Turkmen part of the Caspian Sea.
The Chirag and Azeri oilfields are under development by an $8 billion multinational group, the Azerbaijan International Operating Co (AIOC), which works in cooperation with Azerbaijan.

Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan are on opposite shores of the Caspian Sea. Some of the five states which border the Caspian say it is a lake and some say it is a sea, a distinction which determines the division of underwater resources.
Russia, Iran, Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan, were due to meet in December 1996 to decide the Caspian's status, but the meeting was cancelled.
AIOC plans to begin production later this year and to produce more than 700,000 barrels per day by 2010.
